papers.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
papers.abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Wa\.zewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal annuli in convex balls
papers.abstract: We construct a $4$-parameter family of properly embedded genus-zero surfaces with at most two boundary components in a Riemannian $3$-ball. The construction is a free boundary analog of the canonical $5$-parameter family of surfaces on the $3$-sphere by Marques-Neves in the proof of Willmore conjecture. In the Euclidean unit ball, this family realizes the critical catenoid as a Simon-Smith min-max limit. As applications, we give an upper bound of Almgren-Pitts $4$-width $\omega_4(\mathbb{B}^3)$ by the area of the critical catenoid. Moreover, we prove the existence of at least three free boundary minimal annuli in any compact $3$-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature and strictly convex boundary.

papers.title: There is only one transitive Anosov flow (in dimension 3, with orientable foliations, up to bicontact padding and Goodman surgeries)
papers.abstract: We introduce a new surgical operation on Anosov flows, which we call bicontact padding surgery. The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. Together with previous results, this implies that every transitive Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a suspension flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. This gives some progress towards the Christy-Fried-Ghys conjecture, which predicts that the same statement is true using only Goodman surgery.

papers.title: Convergence of the Calabi flow on K\"ahler surfaces with bounded Sobolev constants
papers.abstract: We study global Calabi flows $g(t)$ on compact K\"ahler surfaces with a uniform Sobolev constant. For any sequence $t_j\to\infty$, set $g_j(t):=g(t_j+t)$. After passing to a subsequence, these flows converge to an eternal Calabi flow on a compact extremal K\"ahler orbifold surface. The convergence holds in the spacetime $\hat C^\infty$-Cheeger--Gromov topology: it is uniform in the Gromov--Hausdorff sense on compact time intervals and smooth away from the orbifold singularities, using comparisons fixed in time.

papers.title: Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures
papers.abstract: We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits. We also establish that no nonzero abelian length function can occur in the holonomy boundary of any such fixed surface, regardless of the limiting quadratic differential. Finally, we characterize all directional boundary fibers by a necessary-and-sufficient analytic condition involving valued representations and the holomorphic jet bundle underlying an oper.

papers.title: Complete Topological Invariant and Coding of Homoclinic Flows on the Two-Dimensional Sphere
papers.abstract: We study codimension one homoclinic flows on closed surfaces and introduce a complete topological invariant based on the structural graph of the flow and the distinguishing graphs of its atoms. This invariant completely determines the topological equivalence class of a homoclinic flow. For flows on the two-dimensional sphere, we construct a canonical coding algorithm that avoids the global renumbering required in the classical coding of Morse flows and substantially reduces the computational complexity. As an application, we derive recursive formulas for the number of topologically distinct homoclinic flows on the two-dimensional sphere and compute these numbers for flows with a small number of saddle singularities and closed orbits.

papers.title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: Let $p>3$ and let $\Gamma$ be a non-elementary Gromov hyperbolic group with $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. We prove that every $\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$-convex cocompact representation $$ \rho:\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PO}_{p,3} $$ whose proximal limit set $\Lambda_\rho\subset\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$ is a $C^1$ submanifold preserves a totally geodesic copy of $\mathbb{H}^p\subset\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$. Consequently, $\Gamma/\ker \rho$ is virtually a cocompact lattice in $\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^p)$. For odd $p$, we prove the same conclusion for every signature $(p,q)$ with $p>q\ge2$, under the same hypothesis $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. Our methods combine dynamics, differential topology, and representation theory. The key new ingredient is to study the radicals of the semidefinite forms induced on the tangent spaces of the limit set. They form a continuous vector bundle of constant rank. The tangent action at attracting fixed points gives a bound, in terms of the radical rank, on the number of eigenvalues of an orthogonal lift whose modulus exceeds one. We then use the topology of the sphere and the representation theory of real algebraic groups to exclude the remaining possibilities. In arbitrary signature with $p>q$, these arguments already imply that a representation with a $C^1$ limit set cannot be Zariski dense.

papers.title: Dimension bounds for finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most $81$, substantially improving Prokhorov's bound of $995$. A refinement of Prokhorov's method gives the intermediate bound $162$, while an extension of Vinberg's planar-angle comparison to the finite-volume setting yields the sharper bound. Both arguments combine improved weighting functions with estimates using cusp geometry to control weight contributions of angles at ideal vertices or edges incident to them.

papers.title: The rigidity of Doyle circle packings on the infinite hexagonal triangulation
papers.abstract: Peter Doyle conjectured that locally univalent circle packings on the hexagonal lattice only consist of regular hexagonal packings and Doyle spirals, which is called the Doyle conjecture. In this paper, we prove a rigidity theorem for Doyle spirals in the class of infinite circle packings on the hexagonal lattice whose radii ratios of adjacent circles have a uniform lower bound in one fixed lattice direction. This gives a partial answer to the Doyle conjecture. Based on a new observation that the logarithm of the radii ratio of adjacent circles is a weighted discrete harmonic function, we prove the result via the Liouville theorem for discrete harmonic functions. Moreover, we establish a Ring Lemma for locally univalent circle packings with bounded degree, assuming that their carrier surfaces are the universal covers of $\mathbb{C}-\{0\}$, and the visual angles of all circles viewed from the origin are uniformly bounded away from $\pi$. This provides a new geometric sufficient condition for the rigidity of Doyle spirals.

papers.title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
papers.abstract: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 \pi^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 \pi^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.

papers.title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
papers.abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.

papers.title: A nonarithmetic lattice from a mirror in the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga construction
papers.abstract: We prove that the stabilizer of a reflection mirror of the Couwenberg-Heckman-Looijenga lattice $\mathcal{C}(G_{29},3)$ induces a nonarithmetic lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$. This lattice is not commensurable with any Deligne-Mostow lattice in $\operatorname{PU}(2,1)$ or any lattice in the twenty-two nonarithmetic classes listed by Deraux, Parker and Paupert.

papers.title: Quantitative spectral rigidity for negatively curved manifolds and Outer Space
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed manifold with fundamental group $G$. A subset of conjugacy classes $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$ is said to be spectrally rigid if when two negatively curved Riemannian metrics have the same marked length spectra on $E$, then their length spectra agree on all conjugacy classes. In this work we study spectrally rigid subsets from a quantitative perspective. We show that, if the density of $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$, measured with respect to a fixed reference metric, decays more slowly than $T^{-1/2}$ then $E$ is spectrally rigid. We establish analogous rigidity results for Culler-Vogtmann Outer Space and show that the $T^{-1/2}$ threshold is sharp in this setting.

papers.title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

papers.title: Minimal quasisections of circle bundles
papers.abstract: Let $E\xrightarrow{\pi}B$ be an oriented circle bundle over an oriented closed surface, and let $\mathcal E$ denote its Euler number. A \textit{quasisection} is a smooth surface $Q$, possibly with boundary, together with a generic smooth map $q:Q\to E$ such that $\pi\circ q(Q)=B$. The \textit{local formula} expresses the Euler number $\mathcal E$ of a bundle as a sum of the weights of the \textit{singular vertices} of a quasisection. In the present paper determine the minimal number $\mathcal N$ of singular vertices for closed and for bordered quasisections for a given circle bundle. For bordered quasisections, \[ \mathcal N_{\mathrm b}(E\to B) =\left\lceil\frac{3|\mathcal E|}{2}\right\rceil. \] For closed quasisections, If $\mathcal{E}$ is even, \[ \mathcal N_{\mathrm cl}(E\to B) =\frac{3|\mathcal E|}{2}. \] If $\mathcal{E}$ is odd, \[ \mathcal N_{\mathrm cl}(E\to B) =4|\mathcal E|. \] We also provide examples of quasisections that realize these minimal values.

papers.title: On the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several nonvanishing results for Floer lasagna modules $\mathcal{FL}(W,K)$ for a smooth compact connected oriented $4$-manifold $W$ and a knot $K\subset \partial W$, via the evaluation maps to link Floer homology. We first establish a general criterion: if a certain Heegaard Floer cobordism map associated with a smooth $4$-manifold $W$ is nonzero, then $\mathcal{FL}(W,U)\neq 0$, where $U\subset \partial W$ is a local unknot. Applications include the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules for $\#^m\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ and for knot traces $X_n(K)$ when $K$ is slice and $n$ is a non-positive integer. In another direction, we show that for every nontrivial knot $K$ and every integer $n$, the Floer lasagna module $\mathcal{FL}(X_n(K),K_n)$ is nonzero, where $K_n\subset S_n^3(K)$ is the dual knot. Moreover, if $K$ is an L-space knot, then $\mathcal{FL}(X_n(K),K_n)$ is infinite-dimensional for all integers $n\ge \max\{2g(K),1\}$.

papers.title: Casson invariant of knots defined by random braids
papers.abstract: We investigate the expectation $E(v_2)$ of the Casson invariant $v_2$ for knots represented by two similar types of braids, the rosette $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $\prod_{1\leq 2i\leq s}\sigma_{2i}^{\pm 1}\prod_{1\leq 2i+\leq s}\sigma_{2i+1}^{\pm 1}$ and the quasitoric $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $\sigma_{1}^{\pm 1}\sigma_{2}^{\pm 1}...\sigma_{s-1}^{\pm 1}$. If $k$ is of the form $ns+1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{s+1}{24}$ where $c$ is the number of crossing points of braid; if $k$ is of the form $ns-1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{5-s}{24}$.\\ If we go through all $3$-braids, regardless of the shape of their diagram, we get $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{8}$. \\ For knots with a checkerboard diagram, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{16}$.

papers.title: Lehmer's number is not an orientable stretch factor in genus six
papers.abstract: Let $\lambda_L \approx 1.17628$ be Lehmer's number. We prove that no pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus six with orientable invariant foliations has stretch factor $\lambda_L$. This gives a negative answer to a question of Lanneau and Thiffeault on the minimal stretch factor in even genus. As a consequence, the minimal stretch factor $\delta_6^{+}$ of such maps is the largest root of $x^{12}-x^{9}-x^{7}+x^{6}-x^{5}-x^{3}+1$, approximately $1.20189$. The proof combines the Lefschetz method of Lanneau and Thiffeault, the standardly embedded train tracks of Hironaka and Tsang, an elementary analysis of the transition digraph, and an obstruction from periodic conjugacy classes in the fundamental group.

papers.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $\pi_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2\pi/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle \tau\rangle$, where $\tau$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.

papers.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
papers.abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

papers.title: Braided Multisections and Aspherical Stein Fillings
papers.abstract: We construct Stein fillings diffeomorphic to complements of a connected symplectic unbranched multisection and a regular sphere fiber in the ruled surface $\Sigma_g\times S^2$. For every $g\geq2$ and every multisection degree $p\geq4$, a fixed contact three-manifold admits infinitely many pairwise nonhomeomorphic aspherical fillings of this form. Their first and second integral homology groups are $\Z^{2g}\oplus\Z/p$ and $\Z^{(2g-1)(p-1)}$, respectively, and their intersection pairings vanish. We vary the braid monodromy while preserving the marked contact boundary. Unbounded torsion orders in the first homology of regular unbranched covers of degree $p2^{p-1}$ detect infinitely many isomorphism types of fundamental groups. We also give an equivariant Weinstein handle construction for the cyclic filling $W_{g,4}$. The contact boundaries are supported by spinal open books with planar pages and have positive ordinary support genus.

papers.title: Relative trisection maps on 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that for an arbitrary compact orientable smooth $4$--dimensional manifold $M$ with a given open book structure on the boundary $\partial M \neq \emptyset$, which may be disconnected, there exists a generic smooth map of $M$ onto the $2$--disk which gives a relative trisection on $M$ consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$. This gives a new proof to the existence of a relative trisection on $M$. In fact, it turns out that every relative trisection can be obtained in this way. As a byproduct, we also show that $M$ always admits a decomposition into a PALF (positive allowable Lefschetz fibration) over the $2$--disk $D^2$ and a fiber bundle over the circle with a sutured compression body fiber, consistent with the given open book structure on $\partial M$ and with the surface bundle structure of the PALF over $\partial D^2$.

papers.title: Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $\omega$ be a smooth positive density, and let $\mu$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms. For $g\ge2$ and quasimorphisms vanishing on the disc braid group, we obtain an injective map to $C^0$-continuous homogeneous quasimorphisms on $Homeo_0(N_g,\mu)$. We also obtain undistortion criteria in $Homeo_0(N_g)$ and $Diff_0(N_g)$. For $g=1,2$ and every $d\ge2$, we prove $$ \dim\overline H_b^d(Homeo_0(N_g,\mu))=\infty,\qquad \dim\overline{EH}_b^d(Diff_0(N_g,\omega))=\infty. $$ Moreover, $\overline{EH}_b^d(Homeo_0(N_2,\mu))$ is infinite dimensional in every positive even degree $d$. Here $\overline{H}_b^d$ and $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denote reduced bounded cohomology and reduced exact bounded cohomology, respectively.

papers.title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
papers.abstract: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park. When $\gcd(p,q)=1$, so that $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot, the formula is a sum of $pr$ monomials with coefficient $+1$, divided by cyclotomic factors, and its exponents are governed by an elementary counting function on the orbit of $q$ modulo $p$. Because the numerator has no cancellation, we are able to give the degree for all $s$ and a simple non-fiberedness criterion.

papers.title: Partially wrapped contact Fukaya categories of 1-jet spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category of a 1-jet space equipped with a stop, which is an \(A_\infty\)-category of Legendrians equipped with representations of their Chekanov-Eliashberg algebras. This category is invariant under contact isotopies of the stop. We prove a wrapping exact triangle and a generation theorem. When the stop is bounded subanalytic singular isotropic, we prove a Morita equivalence between the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category and a microlocal sheaf category.

papers.title: Pontryagin-Weiss classes and a rational decomposition of spaces of homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We construct a rational homotopy pullback decomposition for variants of the classifying space of the group of homeomorphisms for a large class of manifolds. This has various applications, including a rational section of the stabilisation map ${\rm Top}(d)\rightarrow {\rm Top}$ of the space of homeomorphisms of ${\bf R}^d$ for $d\ge 6$, or a new method to construct topological bundles and detect characteristic classes thereof. Some steps in the proofs may be of independent interest, such as the construction of a nullhomotopy of the twice-iterated stabilisation map for the space of orientation-preserving derived automorphisms of the rational $E_d$-operad, results on recovering boundaries of manifolds from their interior in the context of embedding calculus, or a treatment of tensor products of truncated $\infty$-operads.

papers.title: Pseudo-Anosov Flows: A Plane Approach
papers.abstract: In this text we (re)-tell the theory of pseudo-Anosov flows on 3-manifolds with the orbit space as the central character; via a streamlined framework called {\em Anosov-like group actions}. This brings a simplified and unified perspective, and allows for the import of tools from 1- and 2-dimensional topological dynamics. In so doing, we are able to give a relatively efficient presentation (or re-presentation) of foundational results in the field which appeared over several decades and many papers. We hope that the reader, whether a beginning or more advanced topologist or dynamicist, finds this a welcoming invitation to the rich theory of pseudo-Anosov flows.

papers.title: Extending Goldberg's Exact Sequence to Braid Groups of Graphs and Simplicial Complexes
papers.abstract: For a finite connected simplicial complex $X$, the strand map $\iota_\ast$, from $\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ to $\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_1(X,x_i^0)$, sends a pure braid to the homotopy classes of its strands. A theorem of Goldberg (1973) computes its kernel when $X$ is a closed surface other than $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$: the kernel is the normal closure of the pure braids supported in an embedded disc. We extend this picture to arbitrary finite connected simplicial complexes. Call $X$ $\textit{weakly Goldberg}$ if some contractible subcomplex $X_0\subseteq X$ realises Goldberg's description, $\ker\iota_\ast=\left\langle \operatorname{im}(\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)) \right\rangle$, and $\textit{Goldberg}$ if $X_0$ can moreover be chosen so that $\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ is injective. We prove that the strand map is surjective if and only if $X\not\cong S^1$; that $X$ is weakly Goldberg if and only if its free part is a forest; and that $X$ is Goldberg if and only if it admits an $\textit{admissible tree}$ -- a maximal tree of a scaffold, compatible with the boundary and interior types of the attachments of the free part to the thick components. We also classify the complexes for which the kernel is trivial, settle the exceptional surfaces $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$, and obtain complete answers for manifolds and for graphs. The main tools are a graph-of-spaces decomposition of the configuration space at a point of $X$ and a resolution procedure reducing an arbitrary complex to a simple model.

papers.title: Remarks on some maximal subgroups of $F$ and on the $\vec{F}$-index of knots
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that three maximal subgroups of infinite index in the rectangular subgroup \( K_{(2,2)} \) of the Thompson group \( F \), each containing Jones's \( 3 \)-colorable subgroup \( \mathcal{F} \), can be characterized as stabilizer subgroups. Additionally, we show that the \( \vec{F} \)-index, an elementary knot invariant introduced thanks to Jones's construction of knots from Thompson groups, may increase at most by $4$ after changing the orientation of a knot.

papers.title: The model theory of the curve graph
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a bridge between model theory, geometric topology, and geometric group theory. In particular, we investigate the Ivanov Metaconjecture from the point of view of model theory, and more broadly we seek to answer the general question: why does the curve graph of a surface play such a central role in the study of surfaces and mapping class groups? More specifically, we consider a surface $\Sigma$ of finite type and its curve graph $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$, and we investigate its first-order theory in the language of graph theory. Crucially, $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$ is bi-interpretable with a certain object called the augmented Cayley graph of the mapping class group of the surface. We use this bi-interpretation to prove that the theory of the curve graph is $\omega$--stable, to compute its Morley rank, and to show that it has quantifier elimination with respect to the class of $\forall\exists$--formulae. We also show that many of the complexes which are naturally associated to a surface are interpretable in $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$. This shows that these complexes are all $\omega$--stable and admit certain a priori bounds on their Morley ranks. We are able to use Morley ranks to prove that various complexes are not bi--interpretable with the curve graph. As a consequence of quantifier elimination, we show that algebraic intersection number is not definable in the first order theory of the curve graph. Finally, we prove that the curve graph of a surface enjoys a novel phenomenon that we call interpretation rigidity. That is, if surfaces $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ admits curve graphs that are mutually interpretable, then $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are homeomorphic to each other. Along the way, numerous technical results are obtained.
